subtitle: Regret, reproach, and guessing about the past
words.intro: An Alpine hut has a rule book, one stove and a room with twenty snoring people. It’s where the *Bergwacht* come to look for you, and they will tell you, kindly, what you should have done.

grammar[0].blocks[2].title: Four sentences of regret
grammar[0].blocks[2].text: *Du hättest … sollen* (you should have) · *Ich hätte … müssen* (I ought to have) · *Wir hätten … können* (we could have) · *Hätte ich doch …!* (if only)
grammar[0].blocks[3].title: Words for the practice page
grammar[0].fact: German has a neat word for regret that comes too late: *hätte, hätte, Fahrradkette*, literally “would have, would have, bicycle chain”. It’s a rhyme that means: stop saying if only. A candidate for chancellor once used it on live television.

grammar[1].blocks[0].title: One step further back
grammar[1].blocks[0].note: Same werden; the past form + sein or haben pushes the guess back.

grammar[1].blocks[2].blocks[0].title: Make the guess clear
grammar[1].blocks[2].blocks[1].text: *Morgen fahre ich nach Berlin.* A fixed plan needs no werden.
grammar[1].blocks[3].title: Words for the practice page
grammar[1].fact: The form *Er wird das vergessen haben* is called the Futur II, but it’s used for guessing about the past. Every German parent knows it: *Er wird schon angekommen sein*. It means: don’t worry. Often it’s followed by worrying.

opener.caption: Die Braunschweiger Hütte: Bis hierher kommt man nur zu Fuß.
document.intro: A real sign on the wall of an Alpine hut. *ü. N. N.* means above sea level, *erbaut* is built, and *D.A.V.* is the German Alpine Club. A town in the north of Germany built it, at 2,759 metres in Austria.
document.fact: Many Alpine Club huts were built long ago by a local section from a German city, which still runs them. So up in the Austrian Alps you may find a Braunschweig Hut or a Berlin Hut, quite far from either.
document.tasks[1].instruction: Reproach Max, or guess about him.
reading.title: Am Gipfelkreuz
reading.intro: Max and Lena were to meet at the hut at six. It is now half past eight, it’s snowing, and Lena is sitting by the stove with the hut warden, Frau Moser. Then the door opens. It’s Max, in trainers, and with a very old map.
reading.fact: The German Alpine Club has more than a million members, making it the largest climbing club in the world, with hundreds of huts. *Bergwacht* rescuers are mostly volunteers. And if you are rescued while plainly badly equipped, the bill for the helicopter may be yours.
reading.tasks[1].instruction: Turn each into a reproach, with hätte … sollen or müssen.
